  "description": "Expanded Series Bible II #26 Our Little Business reusable adult small-business slice-of-life idea source. The engine generates premises where an adult {{char}} owns, inherits or starts a small business and employs {{user}} on its small staff, varying the trade, ownership origin, finances, staff roles, community and tradition-versus-change decisions while keeping romance optional rather than the engine.",

    "series": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible II",
    "series_number": 26,
    "category": "Small-Business Slice of Life"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{char}} owns, inherits, purchases or starts a small business — a café, bakery, bookshop, repair bench, inn, studio or another modest operation — and employs {{user}} as part of its small staff. The ongoing roleplay follows the practical and interpersonal work of keeping the business alive: shifts, customers, suppliers, rent, repairs, regulars, family expectations and the recurring question of what the business should become. {{char}} works the business personally rather than directing it from afar, and success, modest stability or honest failure all remain open outcomes. Romance between {{char}} and {{user}} is an optional development that employment itself never creates.",
  "core_premise": "An adult {{char}} is the hands-on owner of a genuinely small business and {{user}} works there as one of its few staff. The engine is the everyday operation itself — opening and closing, serving regulars, negotiating with suppliers and landlords, fixing what breaks, deciding what to modernise and what to keep — not a workplace backdrop for a predetermined romance. {{char}} may be brilliant at the craft and hopeless at the books or the reverse; the business may be stable, growing, seasonal or failing; {{user}} may be an inherited employee, a first hire or the only other person on the rota. Every economic outcome and every personal development stays open, and employer/employee status never supplies feelings, loyalty or consent.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult slice-of-life roleplay opening. Specify the trade and what the shopfront, workshop or kitchen is like at first glance; how {{char}} came to own it and what that origin cost her; her concrete strengths and blind spots as an owner; {{user}}'s role, hours and established skills without defining his personality; the staff size and who else is on the rota; the business's real financial position; and the neighbourhood of regulars, suppliers, landlord and competitors around it. Establish one playable opening moment — a morning rush, a first day, a broken machine, a rent letter, a viral post or a quiet after-close tally — and let {{char}} respond to it without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings or future. Romance, if any ever develops, must grow from mutual adult choice rather than the premise.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Business type: café, bakery, bookstore, game shop, florist, repair shop, inn, restaurant, convenience store, hobby shop, bar, studio, or another small operation",
    "How {{char}} came to own it: inherited family business, purchased existing shop, dream startup, side hustle that became real, or an accident of debt and obligation",
    "Whether {{user}} already worked there under a previous owner, is newly hired, is the first-ever employee, or is the only other staff member",
    "{{char}}'s concrete strengths and weaknesses as an owner: craft skill, bookkeeping, customer manner, delegation, pricing and nerve",
    "{{user}}'s established job skills and role on the rota without defining his personality or feelings",
    "Staff size and division of duties, from a two-person shop to a handful of part-timers and weekend help",
    "Financial health: stable, growing, seasonal, break-even, or struggling against rent and suppliers",
    "The surrounding web of regular customers, suppliers, landlord, local competition and involved family members",
    "Tradition versus modernisation: recipes, methods, signage, cash habits, websites, delivery platforms and automation",
    "The setting and neighbourhood: village high street, urban corner, tourist town, market district or small-town main road",
    "How {{char}} and {{user}} met and what their working relationship is like at the opening moment",
    "The single concrete problem or event the opening scene turns on: a review, inspection, broken machine, viral post, cancellation or first day",
    "{{char}}'s life outside the business: home, friendships, hobbies and what the shop has displaced",
    "What long-term growth would even mean here — second location, more staff, better margins or simply surviving — without assuming it happens",
    "Whether any romance between {{char}} and {{user}} exists, stirs, or never begins at all",
    "Potential long-term outcomes left open: prosperity, modest stability, sale, closure or transformation of the business"
  ],
  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour, or whether a seduction succeeds unless the source explicitly supplies that fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth; keep assumptions, cover stories, reputation and objective ground truth distinct where relevant.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Leave cooperation, refusal, quitting, romance, loyalty, expansion, sale and closure open.",
    "All romantic or sexual characters are adults.",
    "Marriage, cohabitation, room sharing, travel, confinement, family relationships, financial payment, and occupational roles do not create romantic or sexual consent.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase a character's baseline personality, goals, nonsexual interests, judgement, or boundaries.",
    "Keep the business small enough that {{char}} is personally involved in day-to-day work rather than acting as a distant corporate executive.",
    "Owning the business does not automatically make {{char}} competent at every aspect of running it; generate her strengths and blind spots independently.",
    "Employer/employee status does not create romance, sexual access, loyalty or {{user}}'s feelings.",
    "Failure, modest stability and gradual improvement are all valid; do not force every business into spectacular success or constant crisis.",
    "Do not treat customers, suppliers or staff as props; give regulars, family and rivals their own adult lives and interests.",
    "Family involvement in an inherited business is help, hindrance or both, but never automatic authority over {{char}}'s decisions.",
    "Financial trouble is a practical problem, not a moral failing or proof {{char}} is incompetent.",
    "Modernisation is not objectively superior to tradition, and tradition is not objectively superior to modernisation; both carry real tradeoffs.",
    "Keep the default setting grounded and ordinary unless a generated variant deliberately chooses a period or fantastic flavour.",
    "Do not assume {{user}} is devoted to the business, plans to stay, or dreams of owning it; his ambitions are his own and unwritten.",
    "If romance develops, it must arise from mutual adult choice independent of employment, and rejection or absence of romance is equally valid.",
    "Keep intimacy, if any, non-graphic and grounded in the everyday texture of the trade.",
    "Optional crossover: SC-54 Subtitles Included can seed the business as a licensed adult-media localisation startup, and SC-05 Vibe-Coded Homework's tooling debate can recur in the shop's own tech decisions.",
    "Vary ownership origin, trade, finances and staffing independently so premises are not cosmetic variations of one shop.",
    "Do not make every landlord, bank and competitor villainous; ordinary, negotiable adults make better drama than cartoon obstacles.",
    "The opening should present a playable working moment, not a completed history of the business.",
    "Overlap boundary: Distinct from Bible I Workplace Stories because the ongoing objective is operating and developing the small business itself, not merely sharing a workplace."

    "All characters, including every staff member, customer and regular, are adults.",

  "raw_prompt": "Generate a non-graphic adult character-card premise for Our Little Business. Adult {{char}} owns, inherits or starts one small business — café, bakery, bookshop, florist, repair bench, inn, bar, studio or similar — and employs {{user}} on its small staff. Establish how she came to own it, her strengths and blind spots as an owner, {{user}}'s role and skills without his personality, the staff size, the real financial position, and the web of regulars, suppliers, landlord, rivals and family. Open on one playable working moment. Non-negotiables: all characters are adults; employment never creates romance, loyalty or consent; romance is optional and mutual or absent; the business may succeed, stabilise or fail, with no outcome predetermined; do not script {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or future; keep intimacy non-graphic; the engine is operating the business itself, not a shared workplace."
